title: On Breathing the cold air deeply
subtitle: 健康医疗 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 健康医疗（人与自我·生活与学习·健康的生活方式、个人安全与自救）
meta: 主题语境：健康医疗（人与自我·生活与学习·健康的生活方式、个人安全与自救）　|　核心词汇：breathe　|　正文 332 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 breathe 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1975 the observer ① breathed the cold air deeply in public, and every assistant in the observatory said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three nights on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the observer ② breathes the cold air deeply in silence without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ breathe the cold air deeply at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ breathed the cold air deeply before — a line in the log for November 1969 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Breathing the cold air deeply in public, the observer said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the lens at the far dome, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ breathe for a moment before answering in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Breathe for a moment before answering at once and never mention it again.

By 1982 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the log, and a new assistant from the next observatory ⑧ breathes for a moment before answering in public every night without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the dome, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ breathed the cold air deeply again when nobody else would.

⑩ To breathe the cold air deeply, my mother said in 1987, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the observatory remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the observatory forgets, somebody breathes the cold air deeply in silence again and somebody must breathe the cold air deeply in public all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 呼吸（一般过去式 breathed the cold air deeply：1975 年观测员头一回这样做，当着众人面）
B. v. 呼吸（一般现在 breathes the cold air deeply：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 呼吸（不定式 to breathe the cold air deeply：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 呼吸（过去完成时 had breathed the cold air deeply：1969 年十一月的观测记录上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 呼吸（动名词 breathing the cold air deeply 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 歇口气（breathe for a moment before answering：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去歇口气答话前的一小会儿）
G. v. 歇口气（breathe for a moment before answering：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 呼吸（后段两处：新来的助手照例 breathes for a moment before answering，而母亲又一次 breathed the cold air deeply）

answers.why: breathe 意为“呼吸”，1975 年观测员当着众人面呼吸深深地吸那口冷空气，那是观测站里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 breathed。
breathe 意为“呼吸”，自那以后观测员一言不发地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 breathes。
breathe 意为“呼吸”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯呼吸深深地吸那口冷空气”，此处为不定式 to breathe the cold air deeply。
breathe 意为“呼吸”，观测记录里 十一月 那行字说明早在 1982 年之前就有人呼吸过，故用过去完成时 had breathed。
breathe 意为“呼吸”，观测员说“呼吸深深地吸那口冷空气这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 breathing the cold air deeply 作主语。
breathe 意为“歇口气”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去歇口气答话前的一小会儿”，should ever 之后用原形 breathe for a moment before answering。
breathe 意为“歇口气”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻歇口气答话前的一小会儿（breathe for a moment before answering at once），以后再也不要提起。
breathe 意为“呼吸”，新来的助手每个夜晚都照例歇口气答话前的一小会儿，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 breathes。
breathe 意为“呼吸”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次当着众人面呼吸深深地吸那口冷空气，用一般过去式 breathed 叙述。
breathe 意为“呼吸”，结尾那句是母亲 1987 年的话：要呼吸深深地吸那口冷空气，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和观测站记住的那一件。

items: 1975 年，观测员当着众人面呼吸深深地吸那口冷空气；观测站里每一个助手都说这是头一回。（breathed the cold air deeply）
多年以后，观测员仍一言不发地做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（breathes the cold air deeply）

早在 1969 年就有人呼吸深深地吸那口冷空气，十一月那天观测记录上的一行字就是证据。（had breathed the cold air deeply）
观测员说过，当着众人面呼吸深深地吸那口冷空气这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（breathing the cold air deeply 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻歇口气答话前的一小会儿，以后再也不要提起。（breathe for a moment before answering，祈使句）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 breathe 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1975 the observer breathed the cold air deeply in public, and nobody in the observatory forgot it.
Even now the observer breathes the cold air deeply in silence whenever the observatory asks.
Breathing the cold air deeply in public, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever breathe for a moment before answering in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new assistant from the next observatory breathes for a moment before answering in public every night, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother breathed the cold air deeply again, and the observatory remembered that half.
